griha-pravesh.summary: A family ceremony marking entry into a new home with prayer, purification and gratitude.
griha-pravesh.purpose: Families commonly seek blessings for harmony, wellbeing and a considered beginning in the new space.
griha-pravesh.when: The date and muhurta should be confirmed for the family, place and tradition.
preparations: Family gotra and sankalpa details if known
Water, flowers, fruit and common puja vessels
confirmWithPurohit: Whether Vastu Shanti or Havan is included
The final samagri list and who arranges it
griha-pravesh.sourceNote: General preparation guidance; the officiating Purohit confirms the final vidhi.

satyanarayan-puja.summary: A widely observed worship of Bhagwan Vishnu, often undertaken in gratitude or around a family milestone.
satyanarayan-puja.purpose: The puja centres devotion, truthfulness and gratitude, and commonly includes katha and prasad.
satyanarayan-puja.when: Often observed on a full-moon day or family-selected occasion; confirm locally.
satyanarayan-puja.sourceNote: General orientation only; practices vary by region and sampradaya.

vivah-sanskar.summary: Hindu wedding rites conducted according to family, regional and sampradaya traditions.
vivah-sanskar.purpose: The ceremony solemnises a shared household and family responsibilities through sacred vows and witnessed rites.
vivah-sanskar.when: A family-specific muhurta and ceremony sequence must be established with the Purohit.
preparations: Both families’ tradition and gotra details
A ceremony timeline shared with vendors
Ritual materials confirmed well in advance
confirmWithPurohit: Language and explanations for the couple
vivah-sanskar.sourceNote: Wedding traditions vary materially; this guide is deliberately non-prescriptive.

ganesh-puja.summary: Worship of Bhagwan Ganesha, commonly performed at the beginning of an undertaking or ceremony.
ganesh-puja.purpose: A devotional beginning seeking clarity and the removal of obstacles.
ganesh-puja.when: Can accompany a new beginning; timing and sequence depend on context.
ganesh-puja.sourceNote: Preparation summary reviewed for a cautious, general consumer introduction.

ganesh-chaturthi.dateLabel: Date varies by location and calendar convention
ganesh-chaturthi.summary: A celebration of Bhagwan Ganesha marked by worship, community gathering and devotional offerings.
ganesh-chaturthi.significance: The observance honours wisdom, auspicious beginnings and the removal of obstacles.
observances: Offerings such as modak according to family practice
Visarjan according to the chosen observance period
ganesh-chaturthi.regionalNote: Duration, tithi interpretation and visarjan practice vary. Confirm the local date and vidhi with a trusted calendar source and Purohit.
ganesh-chaturthi.sourceNote: General cultural orientation; no date is asserted by this static guide.

navaratri.dateLabel: Nine-night observance; dates vary by tradition and location
navaratri.summary: Nine nights of devotion to the Divine Feminine, expressed through distinct regional and family traditions.
navaratri.significance: Navaratri honours forms of Devi and is observed through prayer, fasting, music, dance and community worship.
observances: Fasting according to health and family custom
Garba, dandiya or regional community traditions
Kanya pujan or other family observances where customary
navaratri.regionalNote: Sharad and Chaitra Navaratri, daily deity associations, fasting practice and culminating observances vary considerably.
navaratri.sourceNote: Intentionally broad to respect regional and sampradaya differences.

diwali.dateLabel: Multi-day festival; dates and principal day vary regionally
diwali.summary: A festival of light observed through worship, family gathering, generosity and renewal.
diwali.significance: Meanings and associated narratives differ across regions and traditions, with light representing knowledge and hope.
diwali.regionalNote: The sequence, deities worshipped and calendar day used are not uniform across India. Confirm local practice.
diwali.sourceNote: A non-exhaustive, plural description for discovery.
